turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning! I'm going to go over some questions to make sure we're all set for your surgery today. First, can you tell me a bit about why you're having this knee surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Ah, yes. I've been having a lot of pain in my left knee, especially when I bend it. The doctor said there's a torn meniscus, so they need to go in and clean it up with the arthroscopy lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for sharing that. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and has it been affecting your daily activities?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: About six months now. It's been getting worse, especially when I walk or climb stairs. I can't exercise like I used to, which is frustrating because I try to stay active.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: I see. Now, let's go over your medications. You're currently taking Montelukast 10 mg daily and using a Salbutamol Inhaler as needed. And you've stopped Atorvastatin 20 mg daily?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, that's right. I take the Montelukast every evening for my asthma, and the inhaler when I need it. I stopped the Atorvastatin a few weeks ago as advised.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Got it. Now, regarding allergies — your records say 'no known allergies', but I always like to confirm directly. Have you ever had any reactions to medications, foods, or other substances like latex?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, actually, I think I do have a latex allergy. I found out during a previous check-up. When I had a glove on my hand, my skin got really itchy and red. The doctor said it was a confirmed latex allergy.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that — it's very important for us to know. We'll make sure all the staff are aware and use latex-free equipment. Now, have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, this is my first time. I've never been under general anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about that part.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's completely normal. We'll make sure you're comfortable and explain everything beforehand. Now, are you NPO — that is, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I stopped eating and drinking after midnight, like the instructions said. Just a bit thirsty now, but I'm managing.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great, thank you. Lastly, how would you describe your overall fitness level? Are you able to walk up a flight of stairs or do light housework without getting overly short of breath?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can walk up stairs, but I do get a bit breathless, especially if I go too fast. My asthma is mild, and I only use the inhaler when I'm exercising or if it's dusty.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for all that information. We'll make sure your asthma is well-controlled during the procedure. We're planning for general anesthesia with a femoral nerve block to help with pain after surgery. Any questions from your side?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that covers it. I'm just ready to get this done and start recovering.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. We'll take good care of you. You'll meet the anesthesiologist shortly, and they'll go over the nerve block and anesthesia plan in more detail. Feel free to ask any questions then too.
